column1: # Parity normalisation map: how the derived tree (r5-ha-addon) is read in the canonical tree's
# (a290-ha-addon) names before the two are diffed. Read by scripts/parity_check.py; ADR 0001.
# Columns, tab-separated: kind, scope, pattern, replacement, why.
#   side          scope canonical|derived; pattern = marker file that identifies that tree;
#                 replacement = the label used in expected.tsv's side column
#   define        pattern = NAME; replacement = regex text substituted for <NAME> in later rows
#   path          regex on the derived file's path -> canonical path. Always scope `*`: a
#                 scope names canonical paths, but a path rule rewrites derived names before
#                 any canonical path exists, so a scoped path rule is refused (exit 2)
#   legacy        content rewrite: r5's Topolino65-compatible names -> a290's. Expected to go:
#                 r5 moves to a290's names in one migration release (ADR 0001), and each
#                 rule is deleted once r5 no longer uses that name
#   identity      content rewrite: names that differ only because the car differs
#   verbatim      files that must be byte-identical: compared raw, never normalised
#   skip          files never compared (each repo's own copy of this map and its list)
#   collapse-ws   Python only: runs of whitespace BETWEEN tokens collapse to one space before
#                 comparing; string literals and comments are kept exact (tokenized, so
#                 "Charging  Power" never equals "Charging Power"); indentation is kept
#   ignore-blank  whitespace-only lines are not differences
# Scopes are globs on the CANONICAL path: `*` all, `a,b` only these, `!a,b` all but these.
# Two files in one tree that land on the same canonical path (after the path rules) stop the
# run with an error naming both, since one of them would otherwise never be compared.
# Content rows apply in file order to the derived text only; a replacement never spans a
# line, so a reported line number is the derived file's own. Order matters: legacy before
# identity, because the identity rule for the r5_ prefix would otherwise consume them.
# Adding a rule here hides every difference it rewrites, in every file. A rule belongs here
# only if the two names mean the same thing everywhere; anything narrower is an expected.tsv
# entry, where it is counted. The audit that produced these rules (2026-09-26) checked they
# leave known real differences visible: MQTT_KEEPALIVE, PESSIMISTIC_ENDPOINTS, cabin
# temperature, COMMAND_DEBOUNCE_S and r5's Cabin Temp card all still reach the diff.
